newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cambodia, Laos, Burma growth seen at 6-8 percent.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia, Laos, Burma growth seen at 6-8 percent.

text.p: Annual growth in Laos, Cambodia, and Burma should average around six to eight percent in the next few years, a United Nations unit said on Wednesday.

Gross domestic product growth between 1996 and 2000 should average 8.3 percent for Laos, 7.1 percent for Cambodia and six percent for Burma, the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) said on Wednesday in its 1997 survey.

Categorised by ESCAP as among the Asia-Pacific region's least developed countries, the three nations are expected to join the booming ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) grouping soon, possibly this year.
Earlier this month Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said ASEAN would decide by July whether to admit them.
The ESCAP report said the countries were among those which "can expect to benefit from a continuing structural differentiation of the economies of the region."
Such countries may "have an opportunity to enhance production and exports of labour-intensive and low-tech industries where their comparative advantages are greater," the report said.
"They have to concentrate on strenthening their infrastructures and expanding their educational bases as these are basic requirements for exploiting such opportunities," it added.
The report was released through Singapore's Trade Development Board.
